[🌷] Disable flaky Custom Tabs and PageInfo tests on desktop

These tests flake on Android desktop emulators, and they're part of
why android-internal-desktop-x64-rel needs 3 tries per shard.
Flaky rates below are from CI builders over Oct 12-26:

- CustomTabEngagementSignalsTest (whole class): 7-39% flaky on
  android-desktop-x64-rel-15-tests and 4-15% on
  android-desktop-17-x64-rel-emu-tests, but mostly under 1% on phones.
- PageInfoViewTest#a11yLiveRegionInUserBypass: about 3-5% flaky on
  desktop builders and under 1% elsewhere.

Disable them only on desktop so phone and tablet coverage stays.

[remoting] Re-enable ConnectionTest.Audio and fix NetEq underruns

Reproduced both the pre-stream `CHANNELS_MONO` assertion failure and
the `right_hz > 2050` frequency estimation flake locally and on trybots.

Root causes & fixes:
1. WebRTC's `NetEq` defaults to mono and emits 1-channel silence when
   polled by `WebrtcAudioModule` before the first stereo Opus packet is
   decoded. `FakeAudioPlayer` now ignores `CHANNELS_MONO` packets while
   `data_` is empty.
2. `WebrtcAudioModule` pulls audio using a 30ms wall-clock PLL, whereas
   `TestAudioSource` used an uncompensated 50ms `base::RepeatingTimer`.
   Timer wakeup latency on Mac/Windows caused `TestAudioSource` to fall
   behind, starving `NetEq` and triggering concealment that skewed the
   2000 Hz zero-crossing count. `TestAudioSource` now uses a 20ms timer
   cadence with a 10ms wall-clock PLL.

Verified locally (`--gtest_repeat=20`) and on Linux/ASan/TSan, `mac-rel`,
and `win-rel` trybots with 0 flakes.

[iOS] Re-enable composebox adaptive suggestions EG tests

Re-enables testAdaptiveSuggestionURLSuggestionIsVisible and
testAdaptiveSuggestionSearchBelowURLIsHidden in
composebox_adaptive_suggestions_egtest.mm, which check that adaptive
suggestions keep a high-ranked URL in the last suggestion slot visible
above the keyboard and hide the search suggestion displaced below it.

EarlGrey computes visibility from a rendering of the app's windows; the
software keyboard lives in a separate remote window that is not
rendered, so suggestions covered by the keyboard are reported as
visible. The tests therefore relied on the bottom composebox, which
covered the same area from within the app window. crrev.com/c/8345550
removed the kComposeboxForceTop flag (already enabled by default) and
disabled the tests, and crrev.com/c/8446501 removed the bottom position
entirely so that the composebox is always at the top on iPhone, which
left the tests with no way to detect what the keyboard hides.

Following the approach suggested in crbug.com/556656308,
ComposeboxInttestCoordinator, the test-only coordinator presenting the
composebox, now observes UIKeyboardDidShowNotification and adds an
opaque view covering the keyboard frame to the window of the base view
controller (removed on UIKeyboardWillHideNotification and in -stop).
EarlGrey then considers suggestions under the keyboard as not visible,
matching what the user sees, without relying on the removed bottom
composebox. No other EarlGrey test or test coordinator (such as
OmniboxInttestCoordinator) checks whether UI elements are occluded by
the software keyboard, so this adaptation is kept in
ComposeboxInttestCoordinator rather than extracted into a shared base
coordinator. The kIsOmniboxInBottomPosition pref setup (and the
pref_names dependency) is removed from the test since it no longer
affects the composebox position.

The row matchers also exclude hidden cells with grey_hidden(NO): when
adaptive suggestions reorder the results, UITableView keeps the reused
cell of the previous layout hidden in the view hierarchy with the same
accessibility identifier as the new row, so the matcher matched two
elements and -[ChromeEarlGrey isMatcherSufficientlyVisible:] returned NO
for a fully visible row, picking the wrong URL suggestion index.

No new test is added since this CL re-enables existing tests. Verified
locally on iPhone 16 (iOS 26.5 and 27.0) and on iPad Pro 13-inch (M4)
(iOS 26.5 and 27.0, where the tests skip) with 3 runs per config.

Part of http://go/arthurmilchior-fix-all-test-skill-chrome for AI week.

Reland "[Reading Mode] Fix keyboard navigation and focus restoration for audio dialogs"

This is a reland of commit cf02c83d2457bf23a338166c81233d1aef1148c5

Original change's description:
> [Reading Mode] Fix keyboard navigation and focus restoration for audio dialogs
>
> When opening the Change Accent or Voice Selection dialog from the Voice
> submenu, pressing Escape or ArrowLeft previously closed the underlying
> Voice submenu before closing the dialog, and closing the dialog resulted
> in lost keyboard focus.
>
> This occurred because SettingsMenuElement attaches a capture-phase
> keydown listener on window that intercepted Escape and backward arrow
> keys before the open cr-dialog could handle them.
>
> This CL:
> - Updates SettingsMenuElement.onKeyDown_ to ignore key events
>   originating from inside a CR-DIALOG element.
> - Adds focusItem() to GroupedActionMenuElement to focus a specific menu
>   item by group and item index.
> - Restores focus to the triggering item in AudioMenuElement via
>   GroupedActionMenuElement.focusItem() when the Change Accent or Voice
>   Selection dialog closes.
>
> Keyboard navigation example:
> https://drive.google.com/file/d/1oX0c1J1x2b1JUot1S-zSbpn1Cf2Ai9PC/view?usp=drive_link&resourcekey=0-7dLbnSQgkxSYMgMDY5lTKw

[NTP Customization Sync] Drop a pending daily refresh on theme change

NtpThemeDailyRefreshManager applies a due daily refresh in memory when
the activity is created, and persists it (the rotated Chrome color or
the prefetched theme collection image, plus the refresh timestamp) in
maybeSaveDailyRefreshAndReset() at deferred startup.

If a synced theme or a local selection replaces the persisted background
between these two points, or if the persisted background fails to
initialize, NtpCustomizationConfigManager wipes the SharedPreferences,
but the pending refresh in memory survives. Until deferred startup the
getters keep returning the stale rotation instead of the new background.
Then maybeSaveDailyRefreshAndReset() writes the rotated color id over
the new Chrome color, or runs commitThemeCollectionDailyRefresh() with
the daily refresh data already cleared, which removes the new theme
collection's primary color, and it overwrites the refresh timestamp
either way.

NtpCustomizationConfigManager now discards the pending refresh whenever
it clears the persisted background.

[omnibox] Test real-keyboard text editing in the Full WebUI popup.

The Full WebUI omnibox popup had no test that drives text entry and
editing with real key events. `FullWebUIOmniboxInteractiveTest` types
with `InputWebUIText()`, which sets the input's value from JS and fires
synthetic `input` events; selects all with `SelectAllWebUIInput()`,
which calls `el.select()`; and copies, cuts and pastes with synthetic
`ClipboardEvent`s (`OnCopy` and `OnPaste` only check histograms). None
of these exercise the platform key event routing to the popup widget,
Blink's editing commands, or the system clipboard, and nothing covered
Delete/Backspace at a mid-text caret, Home/End with an inline
autocompletion, or undo/redo. The only parity coverage is for the Views
omnibox (`OmniboxViewTest.BasicTextOperations`, `.Paste`, `.UndoRedo`).

This CL adds the following interactive UI tests, run for both
`WebUIToolbarDisabled` and `WebUIToolbarEnabled`, that send real key
presses (Kombucha `SendKeyPress()`) to the popup:

- RealKeyTypingUpdatesSuggestionsPerKeystroke: after each
  typed character, the WebUI input, the default (verbatim) suggestion
  and the native omnibox text all reflect the new text. Catches typed
  keys not reaching the popup, and suggestions or the native edit model
  not updating per keystroke.
- RealKeyBackspaceAndDeleteAtMidTextCaret: Backspace and
  Delete (Fn+Backspace on macOS) with the caret mid-text delete the
  right character, and the caret stays in place after the updated
  suggestions arrive. Catches results updates resetting the caret, and
  deletions not syncing to the native edit model.
- RealKeyHomeEndAcceptInlineAutocompletion: with an inline
  autocompletion of a typed history URL, End and Home (Cmd+Right/Left
  on macOS) keep the completion as text and move the caret to its end
  or start, and typing continues there. Catches Home/End dropping the
  inline autocompletion or leaving it selected.
- RealKeySelectAllClipboardAndUndo:
  Ctrl/Cmd+A selects all, Ctrl/Cmd+C copies it to the system clipboard,
  Ctrl/Cmd+X cuts it, Ctrl/Cmd+V pastes from the system clipboard at the
  caret, Ctrl/Cmd+Z undoes the pastes and the cut, and
  Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+Z redoes. Catches regressions in the WebUI's
  clipboard handoff to the browser and in its undo/redo history.

[ash] Drop dead //chrome includes from ash code (3/4: apps)

Nine includes across chrome/browser/ash/app_list, app_mode, arc and
system_web_apps name nothing from the header they pull in:
browser_process.h (4), app_service_proxy_factory.h (3) and
profile_manager.h (2).

These three headers were picked because each is only ever reached by
name -- ProfileManager::, g_browser_process, AppServiceProxyFactory:: --
so a file that never writes the symbol cannot be using it. That is not
true of every header: a type held in an auto variable is used without
being named, which is why browser_window_interface.h is left for a
separate pass.

Candidates were removed wholesale, then chrome, unit_tests,
browser_tests and interactive_ui_tests were built, and everything the
compiler rejected was put back. The sweep is split into four CLs by
directory to keep each one reviewable and cheap to revert.

#ai-assisted

[loom] - Hide drag glow when files can't be added as context

Since crrev.com/c/8542810, files dropped onto Omnibox Everywhere are
ignored when AI Mode is unavailable (e.g. for users whose default search
engine isn't Google). But dragging a file over it still showed the drag
glow, which suggests the drop will do something.

The DragAndDropHandler must stay active in that case, so that drops are
still preventDefault()ed and can't navigate the WebContents to the file.
So instead of disabling the handler, map the DRAGGING glow state to NONE
when rendering <search-animated-glow> if canAddFileContext_() is false.
This re-evaluates on every render, so it follows live
updateAimPopupEligibility changes and clears a glow that is already
showing. The is-dragging-file CSS is already gated on
is-fusebox-enabled, so it needs no change.

[DTC] Record collection outcome for OS and profile signals

The OsSignals, BrowserContextSignals and VerifyApps signal collectors
never call LogSignalCollectionSucceeded()/LogSignalCollectionFailed(),
so unlike the other signals they record no per-signal success or
latency histograms. These are exactly the signals collected by the
profile signals report and device trust flows, which left those flows
without per-signal metrics.

Record a collection success (and its latency) in the desktop and
Android OS signals collectors, in the desktop profile signals
collector, and for the Android VerifyApps signal. These collectors have
no failure path once the permission check has passed, so no failure
logging is needed. A SafetyNet failure in the VerifyApps collector
still yields a response and is already tracked by
Enterprise.DeviceSignals.HarmfulApps.Result, so it is not treated as a
collection failure.

The corresponding EnterpriseSignals histogram variants are declared in
the parent CL. The iOS collectors are covered in a separate CL.

AntiVirus and Hotfixes keep being recorded only through the
enterprise.reportingPrivate extension API layer; recording them for the
Windows profile report flow as well would double count the extension
path, and is left as a follow-up.

[DTC] Record collection outcome for iOS OS and profile signals

The iOS OsSignals and BrowserContextSignals collectors never call
LogSignalCollectionSucceeded(), so unlike the other signals they record
neither the per-signal collection outcome histogram nor the latency
histogram, which measures the time elapsed from the start of the
collection until its outcome is known. These are the signals collected
by the profile signals report flow on iOS.

Record a collection success in IOSSystemSignalsCollector and
ProfileSignalsCollectorIOS, along with the collection latency measured
from the start of the collection to the point where the outcome is
recorded. For IOSSystemSignalsCollector this spans the asynchronous
hardware info fetch, so the start time is captured in
GetSignal() and passed along to OnHardwareInfoReceived(); for
ProfileSignalsCollectorIOS the collection is synchronous. Neither has a
failure path once the permission check has passed, so no failure
logging is needed. This mirrors the change made to the desktop and
Android collectors in a sibling CL; the corresponding EnterpriseSignals
histogram variants are declared in the parent CL.

🌺 Revert "[a11y-android] Revert ignored check in IsNodeValid"

This reverts commit 5888953eb792efa4df811f333506ddbe7f659136.
Culprit: 5888953eb792 - "[a11y-android] Revert ignored check in IsNodeValid" (refs/heads/main@{#1727088}, https://crrev.com/c/8651881)

Reason for revert: consistently fails android-16-x64-dbg-tests, android-15-tablet-x64-rel, android-17-x64-fyi-rel, and android-canary-x64-fyi-rel.

Mechanism: 5 tests in WebContentsAccessibilityEventsTest
(test_ariaComboboxDelayShowList, test_ariaTreeCollapse,
test_buttonRemoveChildren, test_menuPopupCreated, test_removeSubtree) in
content_shell_test_apk are consistently failing (4/4 builds across
android-16-x64-dbg-tests #9648, android-15-tablet-x64-rel #10473,
android-17-x64-fyi-rel #2681, and android-canary-x64-fyi-rel #4707,
every attempt (9/9)). Removing !node->IsIgnored() from
WebContentsAccessibilityBase::IsNodeValid allows
WebContentsAccessibilityImpl.buildAccessibilityEvent to emit
TYPE_WINDOW_CONTENT_CHANGED events on ignored nodes whose
AccessibilityNodeInfo is left unpopulated by
PopulateAccessibilityNodeInfo, generating an unexpected
TYPE_WINDOW_CONTENT_CHANGED class_name=android.view.View
[contentTypes=SUBTREE] event when DOM/ARIA updates collapse or remove
subtrees. Please feel free to reland once ignored-node event filtering
or expectations are updated!

WebContentsAccessibilityEventsTest#test_ariaComboboxDelayShowList (and 4
sibling tests in content_shell_test_apk) has failed in 4/4 recent builds
across 4 Android CI builders, every attempt (9/9) in every one of them.
This is not flake: it reproduces on every run, so it blocks the CQ for
every unrelated CL that touches this suite. The regression appears at
refs/heads/main@{#1727088}.

Example failing runs:
https://ci.chromium.org/ui/p/chromium/builders/ci/android-16-x64-dbg-tests/9648
https://ci.chromium.org/ui/p/chromium/builders/ci/android-15-tablet-x64-rel/10473
https://ci.chromium.org/ui/p/chromium/builders/ci/android-17-x64-fyi-rel/2681
https://ci.chromium.org/ui/p/chromium/builders/ci/android-canary-x64-fyi-rel/4707

To run/deflake this test on CQ before relanding, add the following
footer to your CL description:
  Include-Ci-Only-Tests: chromium.android:android-16-x64-dbg-tests,chromium.android:android-15-tablet-x64-rel|content_shell_test_apk

Reverting to green the tree first. Please re-land once the failure is
understood and covered; this revert is about restoring CQ throughput,
not about the merit of the change.

Original change's description:
> [a11y-android] Revert ignored check in IsNodeValid
>
> crrev.com/c/8256250 added `!node->IsIgnored()` to `IsNodeValid` to
> prevent crashes when operating on ignored nodes. However, using this
> check in `WebContentsAccessibilityImpl.handleFocusChanged` causes
> accessibility focus to reset to root during dynamic DOM and SPA
> transitions when nodes are temporarily ignored.
>
> crrev.com/c/8573418 subsequently added explicit ignored-node guards to
> `PopulateAccessibilityNodeInfo`, `UpdateCachedAccessibilityNodeInfo`,
> and `GetSelectionAsTextOffsetsForNode`, while `SetExtendedSelection`
> remains guarded. `IsNodeValid` can therefore safely return to an
> existence check (`GetAXFromUniqueID(id) != nullptr`).
>
> A regression test is added to ensure operations on ignored nodes remain
> properly guarded.
>

pdse: Keep subtitle below title in search engine list dialog

In https://crrev.com/c/8511768, the search engine list dialog header was
switched to a two-column CSS grid to accommodate the "More options"
button.

When the `pickerWithMoreEngines` feature flag is disabled, the button is
hidden, leaving `.title` and `.subtitle` without explicit column
assignments. CSS Grid auto-placement placed `.subtitle` into row 1,
column 2, misaligning it to the right of the title.

This CL explicitly assigns both `.title` and `.subtitle` to column 1 so
they always stack vertically in rows 1 and 2.

[DTC] Add missing EnterpriseSignals histogram variants

GetHistogramVariant() in metrics_utils.cc maps every SignalName to a
histogram variant, but the "EnterpriseSignals" variants block in
histograms.xml only declared the four original signals (AntiVirus,
Hotfixes, FileSystemInfo, SystemSettings). The Agent and Certificates
collectors already record
Enterprise.DeviceSignals.Collection.{Success,Failure}.{Signal}.Latency,
so those samples are currently emitted without any metadata.

Declare the Agent, Certificates, BrowserContextSignals, OsSignals and
VerifyApps variants. The latter three are not recorded yet: follow-up
CLs add the missing LogSignalCollectionSucceeded() calls to the OS,
profile and VerifyApps signal collectors, which are exactly the signals
collected by the profile signals report and device trust flows.

The Success.{Signal}.Items histogram is narrowed to the signals that
actually report a collection size, since the other signals pass no
item count.

blink::StaticBitmapImage: Don't drop HDR metadata on the floor!

A bunch o calls to UnacceleratedStaticBitmapImage::Create didn't specify
HDR metadata, including:
- AcceleratedStaticBitmapImage::MakeUnaccelerated()
- CanvasResourceSharedImage::Bitmap()

A bunch o calls to StaticBitmapImageTransform also dropped the metadata,
including:
- StaticBitmapImageTransform::ApplyUsingPixmap and
- StaticBitmapImageTransform::ApplyWithBlit

Don't do that! Add a test (though this is a salami-slicing where the
heavier testing is coming in the next CLs).

At some point I'm going to want to allow StaticBitmapImageTransform to
apply tone mapping (it will be the fallback path for a bunch of
WebGL/WebGPU texture copy paths). But that's for later.

[searchbox] Render favicon2 default icons as images outside top chrome

cr-searchbox-icon only rendered a chrome://favicon2 `defaultIcon` (a
non-Google default search engine's favicon) as an <img> when
isTopChromeSearchbox is true. Any other searchbox given such an icon
draws the colored favicon as a gray CSS mask silhouette. Omnibox
Everywhere (Loomnibox), which sets isTopChromeSearchbox to false, needs
to match the native omnibox here; passing it the DSE favicon is left to
a follow-up CL.

When the icon is in the searchbox and `defaultIcon` is a favicon URL, it
now behaves the same regardless of isTopChromeSearchbox: the favicon is
used as the image source and shown once loaded (with no match or a
search match), and search_cr23.svg is the mask fallback while it loads
or if it fails. Page URL favicons and the page_cr23.svg fallback stay
top-chrome-only.

No behavior change for existing surfaces: only the top chrome omnibox
popup passes favicon2 default icons today (via
GetDefaultSearchProviderIcon()), SearchboxHandler (NTP realbox) defaults
searchboxDefaultIcon to search_cr23.svg, and Lens uses the Google G.

99b8ca60fafa7768cfaf7dd1ffa0d4028d2e16c3 [ diff ] 
[ContextualTasks] Unshare tabs via controller

Revoking tab access from the tab strip must purge staged, uploaded, and
post-turn server-committed tab context across every cached panel thread
and full-tab AI Mode session in the window. Previously,
`ContextualTasksWebContentsUserData::DeleteTabContext` only removed a
single active attachment token without delegating full `SessionID`
deselection and restored-tab displacement to
`ContextualSearchSessionHandle`.

Implement `UnshareTabs` on `ContextualTasksSidePanelCoordinator` by
delegating per-tab removal through `ContextualTasksWebContentsUserData`
and clearing deselection entries by `SessionID` when tabs are re-shared.

[Sync] Fix OAuthConsumerId in DeviceStatisticsRequestImpl token removal

DeviceStatisticsRequestImpl::Start() requests an access token using
OAuthConsumerId::kSyncDeviceStatisticsMetrics, but in case of auth
errors (net::HTTP_UNAUTHORIZED), passed
OAuthConsumerId::kWebHistoryService to
IdentityManager::RemoveAccessTokenFromCache().

Because OAuth2AccessTokenManager keys its token cache by scope set,
RemoveAccessTokenFromCache() looked up the wrong cache key and left the
cached token untouched, causing the immediate retry to reuse the same
invalid token.

Refactor ShowIdentityNameStateProvider method names and sign-in check

Rename OnUserIdentityChanged() to WaitForImageAndShowIdentityName() and
MaybeShowIdentityName() to MaybeShowIdentityNameWhenImageReady() to
clarify that these methods specifically handle waiting for the account
image before showing the identity name.

verifies the user is still signed in before activating or extending the
greeting.

[SidePanel] Wait for toolbar relayout in side panel tests (2/2)

Wait for the browser control container to be resized for the side panel.
-Previously, #waitForContainerViewOpen and #waitForContainerViewClose
 only waited for the side panel container, which is laid out
 synchronously when the panel opens or closes without animations. The
 browser control container is only re-laid out in a later layout pass.
-Tapping the tab switcher button right after opening the panel could
 race with that relayout and turn into a long press, which is ignored
 on the NTP. This flaked the window-scoped close-all tests at Trip 3.
-Now, both helpers also wait for the control container's width plus
 the side panel's width to match the window width. The check is moved
 out of #changeTheme_retainsBrowserControlContainerWidth into
 #waitForBrowserControlContainerWidth.

[Unified tabstrip] Prevent tab strip scrolling for linux scroll to navigate

Scroll to navigate switches the active tab on scroll events, which already
triggers scrolling the newly active tab into view. We shouldn't let scroll
events directly scroll the tab strip during this and instead only allow
scroll to navigate to update the scroll position via active tab changes.
Also skip recording TabStrip.Horizontal.ScrollSource for mouse and scroll
events when scroll events switch tabs.

parent
3b4aa0efca5ea04ae8291e036f091d7786ff79d8 [ diff ] 
[WebXR] Don't draw the immersive overlay before its graphics are ready

VRBrowserRendererThread restarts the overlay (StopOverlay() then
StartOverlay()) when its draw state changes or its graphics context is
lost, and StartOverlay() creates the GraphicsDelegate asynchronously.
Until it's ready, `graphics_` is null but `started_` is true, and an
overlay pose or frame submission from before the restart can still
arrive:

* SubmitResult() requested the next overlay pose because `started_` was
  set.
* OnPose(), for a pose requested before the restart, called
  graphics_->SetXrViews() on null; only a DCHECK guarded it.

VRUiHostImpl::ShowExternalNotificationPrompt() restarts the overlay this
way in one task when a permission prompt appears while the capture
indicators are showing: it hides the indicators, which stops the overlay,
and then shows the prompt notification, which starts it again. The
overlay draws every frame while the indicators show, so a pose request or
a submission is almost always in flight.

SubmitResult() now requests a pose only once the graphics exist, and
OnPose() ignores a pose that arrives before them. OnGraphicsReady()
already runs the pending overlay update, which requests a new pose.

Revert "Do not activate hidden tabs when dragging a collapsed tab group"

This reverts commit 2efad9e9c931cd6f8971ca616312f7ffc3a7d20d.

Reason for revert:
LUCI Bisection has identified this change as the cause of a test failure. See the analysis: https://ci.chromium.org/ui/p/chromium/bisection/test-analysis/b/5655602631016448

Sample build with failed test: https://ci.chromium.org/b/8666861292623159681
Affected test(s):
[://chrome/test\:interactive_ui_tests!gtest::DetachToBrowserTabDragControllerTest#DragCollapsedGroupHeaderRemainsCollapsed/TabDragging.0](https://ci.chromium.org/ui/test/chromium/:%2F%2Fchrome%2Ftest%5C:interactive_ui_tests%21gtest::DetachToBrowserTabDragControllerTest%23DragCollapsedGroupHeaderRemainsCollapsed%2FTabDragging.0?q=VHash%3Ae92adfe5da7b1ea2)
[://chrome/test\:interactive_ui_tests!gtest::DetachToBrowserTabDragControllerTest#DragCollapsedGroupHeaderRemainsCollapsed/TabDragging.1](https://ci.chromium.org/ui/test/chromium/:%2F%2Fchrome%2Ftest%5C:interactive_ui_tests%21gtest::DetachToBrowserTabDragControllerTest%23DragCollapsedGroupHeaderRemainsCollapsed%2FTabDragging.1?q=VHash%3Ae92adfe5da7b1ea2)
[://chrome/test\:interactive_ui_tests!gtest::DetachToBrowserTabDragControllerTest#DragCollapsedGroupHeaderToSeparateWindow/TabDragging.0](https://ci.chromium.org/ui/test/chromium/:%2F%2Fchrome%2Ftest%5C:interactive_ui_tests%21gtest::DetachToBrowserTabDragControllerTest%23DragCollapsedGroupHeaderToSeparateWindow%2FTabDragging.0?q=VHash%3Ae92adfe5da7b1ea2)
[://chrome/test\:interactive_ui_tests!gtest::DetachToBrowserTabDragControllerTest#DragCollapsedGroupHeaderToSeparateWindow/TabDragging.1](https://ci.chromium.org/ui/test/chromium/:%2F%2Fchrome%2Ftest%5C:interactive_ui_tests%21gtest::DetachToBrowserTabDragControllerTest%23DragCollapsedGroupHeaderToSeparateWindow%2FTabDragging.1?q=VHash%3Ae92adfe5da7b1ea2)
[://chrome/test\:interactive_ui_tests!gtest::TabDragTest#DragCollapsedGroupOverExpandedGroup/All.Horizontal](https://ci.chromium.org/ui/test/chromium/:%2F%2Fchrome%2Ftest%5C:interactive_ui_tests%21gtest::TabDragTest%23DragCollapsedGroupOverExpandedGroup%2FAll.Horizontal?q=VHash%3Ae92adfe5da7b1ea2)
and 4 more ...

If this is a false positive, please report it at http://b.corp.google.com/createIssue?component=1199205&description=Analysis%3A+https%3A%2F%2Fci.chromium.org%2Fui%2Fp%2Fchromium%2Fbisection%2Ftest-analysis%2Fb%2F5655602631016448&format=PLAIN&priority=P3&title=Wrongly+blamed+https%3A%2F%2Fchromium-review.googlesource.com%2Fc%2Fchromium%2Fsrc%2F%2B%2F8614307&type=BUG

Original change's description:
> Do not activate hidden tabs when dragging a collapsed tab group
>
> When dragging a collapsed tab group header within the tabstrip,
> TabDragController was previously selecting all tabs in the group and
> activating the first tab in the group both during drag initialization
> (in ResetSelection) and upon drag completion (in CompleteDrag). Because
> collapsed tab groups are prevented from expanding during a drag, this
> resulted in an invisible tab inside the collapsed group becoming the
> active tab and the previously active tab losing selection.
>
> This CL ensures that neither ResetSelection nor CompleteDrag selects or
> activates tabs in a dragged group if the group is collapsed, keeping the
> existing active tab unchanged.
>
> Also adds assertions to DragCollapsedGroupHeaderRemainsCollapsed in
> tab_drag_controller_interactive_uitest.cc verifying that the active tab
> remains unchanged and that no tab inside the collapsed group is
> activated.
>

[EVP] Add "More" menu to Verified email settings on Android

On Android, each verified email in Settings > Contact info showed the
email with a secondary "Verified by <issuer>" line, and tapping the row
opened a "Remove verified email?" dialog. This did not match the Desktop
UI or the design, which shows a "More" button with a "Remove permission"
menu item on the right of each email.

This CL:
- Adds AutofillVerifiedEmailPreference, a non-selectable row with a
  ListMenuButton widget whose menu has a "Remove permission" item. Like
  the "More" button in the search engine settings list, the button only
  covers the icon so that it fits within the row's padding and lines up
  with the toggles above.
- Removes the "Verified by" summary line.
- Updates the confirmation dialog to match Desktop: "Remove
  permission?", "Going forward, <issuer> will stop automatically
  confirming this email", and a "Remove" button.

The Desktop "Remove permission" strings move from settings_strings.grdp
to components/autofill_strings.grdp with android_java formatting so both
platforms share them. The body is split by platform because Android
needs a %1$s placeholder. The now-unused "Verified by" and "Remove
verified email?" strings are removed.

Screenshot: https://screenshot-v2.corp.google.com/7Nu4y64oLtLdcFy

[AvatarButton] Do not trigger greeting when IPH shows mid-session

ShowIdentityNameStateProvider::OnIPHPromoChanged previously called
ShowIdentityName() unconditionally whenever an IPH anchored to the
avatar button changed state. When the greeting was not active (either
after the startup greeting had already finished or when Chrome started
signed out), showing an IPH mid-session unexpectedly activated the
greeting and subsequently triggered the avatar promo once the greeting
collapsed.

Only extend the greeting animation in OnIPHPromoChanged when
ShowIdentityNameStateProvider is already active.

[MChips] Reduce merchandising chip padding in narrow windows.

With the phone layout, the icon-only optional and incognito buttons use
a 32dp lateral padding, i.e., 88dp wide each. In very narrow windows,
e.g., a side-by-side split screen resized to its minimum width, they
leave too little width for the AI Mode button, whose label is truncated.

This CL moves the 32dp padding into values-w360dp, and uses the default
button margin (8dp, i.e., 40dp wide buttons) for windows narrower than
360dp. Phones in portrait at the default display size (>= 360dp) and
windows >= 600dp (40dp from values-w600dp) are unchanged. Full-screen
windows narrower than 360dp, e.g., small phones or a large display size,
also get the reduced padding, since they have the same space shortage.

The coordinator re-reads this dimension whenever the NTP observes a
display style change, e.g., with the Aurora large padding style used in
the bug.

Screenshot: http://shortn/_xG9epgeExD.

bluetooth: Avoid recreating Floss D-Bus clients when removing adapter

Floss client constructors are blamed in 3.6% of ChromeOS browser
shutdown hang reports. During BluetoothAdapterFloss::Shutdown(),
RemoveAdapter() switches FlossDBusManager to kInvalidAdapter, which
previously called ResetAdapterClients() to destroy the active clients
and immediately construct 9 new Floss*Client instances right before
FlossDBusManager::Shutdown() deleted them.

Clear the adapter clients without allocating replacements when
switching to kInvalidAdapter. Recreate clients lazily if a getter is
called while no adapter is active; any client created that way is kept
and initialized on the next adapter power-on, matching the previous
lifecycle. Also guard BluetoothAdvertisementFloss::Stop() and observer
removal in ~BluetoothDeviceFloss(), ~BluetoothGattConnectionFloss(),
and ~BluetoothGattServiceFloss() when no adapter is active, and guard
~FlossAdvertiserClient() when bus_ is null.

[Clank Multiprofile] Migrate FontSizePrefs to per-profile

FontSizePrefs writes to a profile-scoped PrefService
(webkit.webprefs.font_scale_factor), but previously cached a single
static instance (sFontSizePrefs), causing subsequent
BrowserContextHandle instances passed to getInstance() to be ignored.

Since the native object only wraps a PrefService, replace the cached
instance and its native counterpart with a stateless static
setFontScaleFactor(PrefService) method that passes the profile's
PrefService to native code.

[Android] Stop using deprecated ShadowPackageManager APIs in WebAPK

ShadowPackageManager's resolve-info methods and addPackage() are
deprecated. Register the WebAPK share target and URL handler
activities and the browser activities with intent filters instead of
canned ResolveInfos, and use installPackage() instead of addPackage().

Components are added after installPackage(), which replaces the whole
package. For the same reason, WebApkUpdateManagerUnitTest now updates
the registered WebAPK instead of replacing it.

WebApkValidatorTest keeps one addResolveInfoForIntent() call. It
covers a check for a result from another package, which intent
filters never return.

Test: run_chrome_junit_tests, run_components_junit_tests
Test: run_webapk_{client,shell_apk,shell_apk_h2o}_junit_tests

🌺 Disable unused blame list generation on android-code-coverage

CONTEXT: http://chat/room/AAAAoUXNrGc/-mCWDcmXX9o/-mCWDcmXX9o

`generate_blame_list = True` was enabled on `android-code-coverage` in
https://crrev.com/c/4003998 (Nov 2022, crbug.com/1371204) as an
experiment for author / reporting-chain coverage.

The downstream consumer in `infra/infra` (`author_coverage.py` /
`create_author_coverage.py`) was removed in Oct 2023 in
https://crrev.com/c/4933082 ("Remove author coverage. This feature was
never used."), leaving `android-code-coverage` as the only builder in
Chromium still generating `blame.json`.

On `android-code-coverage` (e.g. build 8164), running sequential
`git blame -e --since=4.weeks` across ~6,747 Java files during both the
`overall` and `unit` coverage metadata passes accounts for ~4h 42m of
the build's ~5.5-hour total runtime after all test shards have already
completed in 58 minutes.

Disable `generate_blame_list` on `android-code-coverage` to eliminate
the unused ~4.7-hour blame pass.

[Public Transit] Delete ChromeTabUtils#selectTabWithAction()

Its 2 callers select tabs differently:
- TabStripTest#selectTab() tests tab strip clicks, so it keeps clicking
  the tab with TabStripUtils.clickTab() and hops on at the selected tab,
  whose page Station waits for the selection.
- BookmarkTabletTest only needs to switch back to a tab, so it uses
  CtaPageStation#selectTabFast(), hopping on at the current tab first.

[visited-url-ranking] Re-enable FetchURLVisitData_AggregateCounts

Re-enable
HistoryURLVisitDataFetcherDataTest.FetchURLVisitData_AggregateCounts,
which was disabled in crrev.com/c/5981981 on the November 3, 2024
Daylight Saving Time fall-back day.

SampleScenario_OverlappingTimeGroup() and
SampleScenario_NonOverlappingTimeGroup() previously computed local noon
by taking local midnight (GetStartOfDay, hour = 0) and adding
base::Hours(12). On a Daylight Saving Time fall-back day, adding 12
elapsed hours to 00:00 local time yields 11:00 AM local time (TimeGroup
1, hours 6-11) rather than 12:00 PM local time (TimeGroup 2, hours
12-17). Consequently, today_mid_of_day + 1h (12:00 PM) and + 2h (1:00
PM) fell into TimeGroup 2 instead of matching today_mid_of_day's
TimeGroup 1, and today_mid_of_day - 1h (10:00 AM) and - 2h (9:00 AM)
fell into TimeGroup 1 instead of the prior time group.

Compute local noon directly by setting time_exploded.hour = 12 before
calling base::Time::FromLocalExploded() in GetNoonOfDay() so that
today_mid_of_day is always 12:00 PM local time regardless of 2:00 AM
DST transitions.

Part of http://go/arthurmilchior-fix-all-test-skill-chrome for AI week.

[Policy] Use 8 PolicyToPrefsMapping chunks on Android

Part of the effort to speed up android_browsertests.

ChunkedPolicyPrefsTest splits JSON policy-to-pref mapping checks across
32 separate browser test cases. On Android, each chunk spawns a fresh
Activity and browser process (~2.8 s overhead per test) even though each
check only takes ~250 ms.

Reduce kNumChunks in policy_prefs_browsertest.cc from 32 to 8 on
Android, eliminating extra browser startups while keeping each chunk
short (~3.8 s on CQ).

Measured impact: On an android-x64-rel CQ dry run, summed GTest time
across ChunkedPolicyPrefsTest drops from 97.3 s (32 chunks) to 30.2 s
(8 chunks, -69% / -67.0 s).

[iOS] Extract the part of getting `WatermarkStyle` from prefs to a util function.

This CL extracts the code where getting `WatermarkStyle` from the
prefService map to an independent util functions so that we can reuse it
for both tab level and tab-grid level watermarking without any code
duplications. The changes include:
 - Added a new watermark_style_util class to extract and clamp styling from the prefService.

 - Added a new watermark_style_utils_unittest
 - Updated the watermark_view_unittest accordingly.

[Android] Stop using deprecated ShadowPackageManager APIs in chrome

ShadowPackageManager's resolve-info methods and addPackage() are
deprecated. Register the activities that the code under test looks
up, with matching intent filters, instead of canned ResolveInfos, and
use installPackage() instead of addPackage().

Filters queried with MATCH_DEFAULT_ONLY get CATEGORY_DEFAULT, as on a
real device.

[Android] Trim browser test APK locales and paks

Previously, android_browsertests packaged all shipping Chrome locale
.pak files (~55 MB uncompressed) into android_browsertests-debug.apk
via chrome_apk_pak_assets, and also duplicated 6 .pak files (~45 MB) in
runtime data pushed to /sdcard/chromium_tests_root/paks/ even though
ResourceBundle and WebUI tests load them from APK assets.

Restrict android_browsertests APK locale .pak assets to the 5 locales
exercised by browser tests (ar, en-GB, en-US, es, he) and remove the
duplicate runtime data .pak entries.

Measured impact: Shrinks android_browsertests-debug.apk from 511 MiB on
main to 463 MiB (-48 MiB / -9.3%) and drops ~45 MB of duplicate pushed
runtime .pak files (-7.7 MiB off the compressed .zst archive per shard).

[ntp-composebox] Prevent vertical shift in tool mode when submit appears

When in tool mode (or when tab context is attached) without a file
carousel, selecting a suggestion or entering text enables the submit
button (`[submit-enabled]`), which has an outer block height of 54px
(12px top margin + 40px height + 2px bottom margin) plus 2px
`padding-block-end` on `#carouselContainer` (56px total).

Previously, `#toolChipsContainer` and `#contextMenuContainer` had
`padding-block-start: 6px` (6px + 36px + 2px = 44px) and
`#carouselContainer` had 0px `padding-block-end` until
`[submit-enabled]` was set, causing the tool chip to jump down by 10px
and the suggestions dropdown to shift down by 12px when the first
suggestion was selected.

Update `#toolChipsContainer` and `#contextMenuContainer` to use
`padding-block-start: 16px` when `:not([show-file-carousel])` (keeping
6px when `[show-file-carousel]` is active to preserve the 18px gap below
the carousel) and apply `#carouselContainer` bottom padding when
`[in-tool-mode]` or `.has-tabs` is active so the action row height
remains a constant 56px before and after the submit button appears.

Screencast of the issue:
https://screencast.googleplex.com/cast/NTk3MzcxOTk3MjMxNTEzNnxlZjdmOGZiMy1lMA

Screencast after fix:
https://screencast.googleplex.com/cast/NTg3NzQ4NjE5Njg4MzQ1NnxlY2YxYTU5Mi1hZg

WaaP: Preserve per-story trace_processor CSV metrics

Crossbench's TraceProcessorProbe writes per-row cb_story metadata to
each <query>.csv file, whereas <query>.json merges values across all
stories via MetricsMerger without cb_story. Reading only the JSON files
caused multi-story benchmarks (such as browser_startup.crossbench) to
collapse all stories into a single default bucket.

This CL updates crossbench_result_converter.py to extract per-story
Histograms from trace_processor query CSV files when available, skipping
their merged JSON counterparts.

[iOS] Send Sec-CH-UA-Full-Version-List in AIM

Populate `Configuration::full_version_list` in
`IOSChromeAimEligibilityServiceFactory` using RFC 8941 structured
header serialization (`net::structured_headers::SerializeList`) and
`version_info::GetVersionNumber()`.

Set `full_version_list` unconditionally before the
`contextual_tasks::kContextualTasks` check (matching Desktop/Android in
https://crrev.com/c/8344090) so `/async/folae` eligibility requests
include the `Sec-CH-UA-Full-Version-List` HTTP header whenever
`kAimServerEligibilitySendFullVersionListEnabled` is enabled, allowing
server-side version gating at milestone/build/patch granularity.

Keep a TODO to replace the local helper with a proper //ios/web API.

ios: Add startup memory footprint to the iOS perf suite

Capture the browser process physical memory footprint in bytes inside
the `TakeStartupMemorySnapshot` deferred initialization block and store
it on `StartupInformation.startupMemoryFootprintBytes`. This matches
the snapshot point used by `Memory.Browser.MemoryFootprint.Startup` and
Hawkeye's `Deferred_Initialization_Blocks_Complete_physicalFootprint`
without the 1 MB UMA bucketing.

Expose `+startupMemoryFootprintBytes` on `PerfAppInterface` and record
`Startup.MemoryFootprint` (`sizeInBytes_smallerIsBetter`) under
`bling.startup` across the 5 cold launches in `-[PerfTestCase
testStartup]`.

[iOS] Re-enable SocketWatcherTest.PrivateAddressRTTNotNotified

Re-enable NetworkQualitySocketWatcherTest.PrivateAddressRTTNotNotified
on iOS, which was disabled in https://crrev.com/c/2311116 due to test
failures when running in the full net_unittests suite.

https://crrev.com/c/2219011 added a process-global flag
g_consider_loopback_ip_to_be_publicly_routable_for_testing in
net/base/ip_address.cc and a unit test
IPAddressTest.ConsiderLoopbackIPToBePubliclyRoutableForTestingMethod
that permanently set the flag to true without resetting it. Because iOS
runs net_unittests in a single process, whenever that test ran before
PrivateAddressRTTNotNotified, IPAddress::IsPubliclyRoutable() returned
true instead of false for the "127.0.0.1" and "::1" loopback test cases,
causing SocketWatcher::ShouldNotifyUpdatedRTT() to return true instead
of false.

https://crrev.com/c/3538065 removed
g_consider_loopback_ip_to_be_publicly_routable_for_testing,
IPAddress::ConsiderLoopbackIPToBePubliclyRoutableForTesting(), and
IPAddressTest.ConsiderLoopbackIPToBePubliclyRoutableForTestingMethod,
ensuring IPAddress::IsPubliclyRoutable() always returns false for
loopback addresses regardless of test execution order.

[Views] Re-enable ContextMenuNoFocusedFrame unit test on Mac

Re-enable
ChromeWebContentsViewDelegateViewsTest.ContextMenuNoFocusedFrame on Mac,
where it was disabled in crrev.com/c/3548436.

In ChromeRenderViewHostTestHarness, web_contents() is not hosted inside
a views::Widget or NSWindow. After crrev.com/c/3247722 changed
ShowContextMenu() to build and show the context menu using the passed-in
RenderFrameHost even when GetFocusedFrame() is null,
RenderViewContextMenuViews::Show() on non-Mac platforms returned early
when GetTopLevelWidget() was null, whereas
RenderViewContextMenuMacCocoa::Show() on Mac still invoked
[NSMenu popUpContextMenu:withEvent:forView:] without a hosting Widget or
NSWindow, causing the unit test to fail.

crrev.com/c/4691867 updated RenderViewContextMenuMacCocoa::Show() (and
crrev.com/c/5259806 did the same in
RenderViewContextMenuMacRemoteCocoa::Show()) to return early when
views::Widget::GetTopLevelWidgetForNativeView() is null, matching
non-Mac platforms and allowing this unit test to pass on Mac.

[ash] Forward-declare Profile, drop profile.h (2/4: login and policy)

Eight files in chrome/browser/ash/login and chrome/browser/ash/policy
include chrome/browser/profiles/profile.h but only ever use Profile as
an opaque pointer: they name it in a signature, or store it in a member,
and pass it along without ever dereferencing it. A forward declaration
is enough, and in each case one is already reachable without this
include.

This is a class the earlier dead-include sweeps could not see. They
asked whether a file names Profile at all, and these files do, so they
were never candidates.

The candidates were picked per directory rather than tree-wide: these
are the directories where every profile.h includer qualifies, so the
chrome/browser/profiles dependency goes away instead of moving to a
sibling file. Two build deps go with them, in
policy/reporting/user_added_removed and policy/skyvault/test.

The compiler decided the rest: candidates were removed wholesale, then
chrome, unit_tests, browser_tests and interactive_ui_tests were built,
and everything it rejected was put back -- nearly all of those passing a
Profile* to a content::BrowserContext* parameter, an upcast that needs
the complete type. The sweep is split into four CLs by directory to keep
each one reviewable and cheap to revert.

omnibox: Enable the WebUI popup deferrals by default on ChromeOS

OmniboxWebUIPopupDeferCreation and OmniboxAimPopupDeferCreation move
the creation of a window's WebUI omnibox popups from the window's
construction to just after its first presented frame. A popup shown
before that is created on that show. The features landed disabled.

Enable both by default on ChromeOS. Session restore at login creates
every restored window at once, so creating the popups with the window
delays the windows themselves. On two 4 GB devices
(ui.LoginPerf.noarc_2windows, 6 interleaved runs per arm, official
build), the deferrals cut TPS.SessionRestore-CreateRestoredBrowser-End
by 26-35% and Ash.LoginPerf.AutoRestore.AllBrowserWindowsPresented by
6-8%, matching the Views popup, with no change in memory or in any
other metric. Both features stay as kill switches.

AddContextButtonVisibilityAndClick waits for the AI Mode content
before opening the popup: the inline "Add Context" button needs that
content, and the location icon refreshes on popup state changes and
typing, not when the content appears. The resource budget test waits
for every presenter to create its content before counting, since the
budget is the state after the first frame. BrowserNavigatorTest
enables the WebUI popups, so its remaining
CreateAndLoadWebContentsObserver calls switch to
AllBrowserTabAddedWaiter to ignore popup WebContents created when the
initial window presents its first frame during the test body.

[ash] Forward-declare Profile, drop profile.h (3/4: apps)

Twenty-three files in chrome/browser/ash/app_list, app_mode, arc and
system_web_apps include chrome/browser/profiles/profile.h but only ever
use Profile as an opaque pointer: they name it in a signature, or store
it in a member, and pass it along without ever dereferencing it. A
forward declaration is enough, and in each case one is already reachable
without this include.

This is a class the earlier dead-include sweeps could not see. They
asked whether a file names Profile at all, and these files do, so they
were never candidates.

The candidates were picked per directory rather than tree-wide: these
are the directories where every profile.h includer qualifies, so the
chrome/browser/profiles dependency goes away instead of moving to a
sibling file. Two DEPS allowances and four build deps go with them, in
app_list/search/common, app_mode/isolated_web_app, arc/adbd and
system_web_apps/apps/vc_background_ui.

The compiler decided the rest: candidates were removed wholesale, then
chrome, unit_tests, browser_tests and interactive_ui_tests were built,
and everything it rejected was put back -- nearly all of those passing a
Profile* to a content::BrowserContext* parameter, an upcast that needs
the complete type. The sweep is split into four CLs by directory to keep
each one reviewable and cheap to revert.

#ai-assisted

[crypto] Remove RSA from the TPM2_Create AIK path

RSA attestation keys are created through the Platform Crypto Provider
again, so only ECDSA AIKs are still built with a raw TPM2_Create. Drop
the RSA support that path no longer needs, and put ECDSA in the names
of the builders:

- unexportable_key_win.cc: replace WindowsSrkHandle and
  GetSrkHandleFor() with a single kEccSrkHandle, drop the RSA check in
  CreateAikUnderTransientSrk(), and map `algo` to a hash with
  ToHashKind() before building the command.
- tpm.rs: build_create_aik_command() becomes
  build_create_ecdsa_aik_command(), loses its scheme parameter and
  always builds an ECDSA key. SHA-1 stays unsupported.
- tpm_parser.cc: BuildCreateAikCommand() becomes
  BuildCreateEcdsaAikCommand() and takes a hash::HashKind instead of a
  sign::SignatureKind. SHA-1 is now a CHECK failure rather than a
  nullopt (callers only pass SHA-256), so it no longer returns
  std::optional.
- Tests: delete the RSA template tests, add a SHA-1 death test, and
  check BuildCreateEcdsaAikCommand() for SHA-256, SHA-384 and SHA-512.

Original change's description:
> [iOS] Fix CloseButton and NavigationBarCloseButton matchers on iOS 27.2
>
> On iOS 27.2 Beta 3, UIKit changed the accessibility label for system
> close buttons (UIBarButtonSystemItemClose and the UISearchBar dismiss
> button on iPhone) from 'Close' to lowercase 'close' on both the outer
> interactive _UIButtonBarButton (userInteractionEnabled=YES) and the
> inner _UIModernBarButton (userInteractionEnabled=NO).
>
> Update +[ChromeMatchersAppInterface closeButton] to match either
> IDS_CLOSE or lowercase 'close' with grey_userInteractionEnabled(), and
> update +[ChromeMatchersAppInterface navigationBarCloseButton] to reuse
> +[ChromeMatchersAppInterface closeButton]. This fixes
> SaveProfileEGTest/testUserData_LocalEditViaBottomSheet and
> TipsPromosTestCase/testSearchWhatYouSeePromo on iOS 27.2 Beta 3.

The original CL broke BookmarksNavigationBarBackButton() on iOS 18.5
because its < iOS 26 fallback uses grey_not(navigationBarCloseButton) to
filter out the inner _UIModernBarButton (userInteractionEnabled=NO).
Gate the updated closeButton and navigationBarCloseButton matchers
behind @available(iOS 26, *) so iOS 18.5 retains the existing behavior.

Reland "[Android] Match InProcessBrowserTest feature list"

This is a reland of commit 231082cd7aaa69d1def498bbefc14f34cdd4e654.

The original CL was reverted in https://crrev.com/c/8640364 due to
deterministic timeouts in WebUI focus, TabBottomSheetBrowserTest, and
SecurePaymentConfirmationTest suites across Android Desktop and Tablet
CI builders.

Local A-B-A reproduction showed those failures were caused by
ScopedIphFeatureList::InitWithNoFeaturesAllowed(), rather than disabling
the background startup features. On tablet and desktop Android,
TabbedRootUiCoordinator.initializeIph() (specifically
BookmarkBarIphController) gates startup bookmark model loading on
Tracker.wouldTriggerHelpUi(); blocking all IPH altered deferred startup
and omnibox URL bar focus timing, suppressing BottomSheetController and
stealing focus from WebContents.

Changes from Patchset 1 (baseline): Remove ScopedIphFeatureList from
AndroidBrowserTest while keeping the four disabled background features
(kPreconnectToSearch, kPrewarm,
kRestartNetworkServiceUnsandboxedForFailedLaunch, and
kTransientKeepAlivePolicy), which provide the startup speedup.

Original change's description:
> [Android] Match InProcessBrowserTest feature list
>
> Previously, AndroidBrowserTest left default search engine preconnect
> (kPreconnectToSearch, which fires with a 0 ms startup delay on Android),
> search engine prewarm (kPrewarm, which warms up a background prerender
> renderer and compositor during startup),
> kRestartNetworkServiceUnsandboxedForFailedLaunch,
> kTransientKeepAlivePolicy, and in-product help features enabled, unlike
> desktop's InProcessBrowserTest.
>
> Disable these background features by default and block IPH via
> ScopedIphFeatureList in AndroidBrowserTest to match
> InProcessBrowserTest, avoiding unnecessary startup overhead and
> nondeterministic background work. Dedicated tests for these features can
> still enable them via ScopedFeatureList or ScopedIphFeatureList.
>
> Measured impact: On a 5-test local android_browsertests batch (5 runs on
> emulator-5554), batch wall time drops from 17.24 s to 16.66 s (-3.4%, or
> -118 ms/test) in default run-from-apk mode and from 15.41 s to 14.86 s
> (-3.5%, or -108 ms/test) after package compilation, with mean GTest
> runtime dropping by 4.4% to 5.2%.
>
> Bug: 576702252
> Test: run_android_browsertests --gtest_filter=AndroidBrowserTest.*

[User Education] Make RecentSessionPolicyImpl GetEndOfDay() DST-safe

GetEndOfDay() computed the start of the next local day as (time +
base::Days(1)).LocalMidnight(). On a 25-hour DST fall-back day, if time
falls between 00:00 and 01:00 local time, adding a fixed 24 hours lands
at 23:xx on the same calendar day, causing LocalMidnight() to return the
start of the current day rather than the next day.

Anchor from time.LocalMidnight() and add 28 hours before rounding down
to local midnight, which is both DST-safe and accurate when time is
exactly local midnight.

[Views] Create ViewGuard to ensure a view's existence in a scope

Sometimes locking down every possible corner case callback that could be
used by a confused or malicious listener to trigger a UAF during some
otherwise innocuous operation isn't worth it if none of the resulting
states would be valid.

ViewGuard provides another option: kill the process if something
unexpected and extremely bad happens. Follows the same principle as
raw_ptr/raw_ref except that the kill still happens immediately if the
destruction occurs in some nested call, and it's therefore often
better-suited for on-the-stack use in Views code.

Migrates the "don't let MenuItemView be destroyed while adding it to a
menu" code added in an upstream CL to the new one-line guard.

displayed until the distilled content has been translated, so users

Fix MultiWindowAppMenuTest group test on Android 12L split-screen

testAddToGroup_showsGroupsFromOtherWindow created the second window's
tab group through that window's tab switcher UI. Since new windows
open in split-screen, on Android 12L the second window's app menu can
be cropped out by the platform when the IME belongs to the first
window, so the "Select tabs" click misses.

Create the group programmatically instead. The test still checks what
it is about: the first window's app menu lists the group from the
other window.

The test stays disabled on 12L for now; it will be re-enabled after
the test reviver confirms the fix.

Don't report a stale Reading Mode close reason

ReadAnythingController::CloseSidePanelUI() saves the close reason before
asking the side panel to close, and OnSidePanelWillHide() reports it to
Reading Mode's lifecycle observers. If the side panel doesn't close
(e.g. it's still loading, or its tab is in the background), the reason
stays saved and is reported for the next, unrelated close instead.

For example, if Reading Mode opens in the side panel, pressing its
keyboard shortcut twice while the side panel loads for the first time
in a tab saves kClosedByUser. The next tab switch is then reported as a
user close instead of kTabSwitched, so observers like PDF translation
treat it as Reading Mode being closed.

This CL clears the saved reason after asking the side panel to close.
If the side panel did close, OnSidePanelWillHide() has already used it.

8bb37448fe6018a1b7acaf5cb4ba1bbfa8444ad1 [ diff ] 
Return String by value from HitTestResult::AltDisplayString()

HitTestResult::AltDisplayString() previously returned a const
AtomicString& referencing the underlying Element's internal attribute
storage. During image drag preparation in
DragController::PopulateDragDataTransfer(),
PrepareDataTransferForImageDrag() updates the selection before
consuming the label string, which can synchronously dispatch a blur
event. If a blur event listener mutates attributes on the dragged image
and reallocates its attribute vector, the borrowed reference becomes
dangling.

Return String by value from HitTestResult::AltDisplayString() (matching
HitTestResult::Title() and HitTestResult::TextContent()) so callers own
a reference-counted String copy that remains valid across synchronous
script execution.

[inline-layout] Reduce glyph-range iterator overhead

Checked glyph iterators add overhead to noncompact glyph-range searches
and safe-break scans, including when monospace compaction is disabled.

Use pointer-backed standard algorithms within validated, read-only glyph
spans. Keep std::lower_bound for LTR ranges and use std::partition_point
to search descending RTL clusters directly, avoiding reverse-iterator
bookkeeping. Share the safe-break scan between directions, using a
pointer-backed reverse view for LTR and checked forward iteration for
RTL.

Preserve cluster boundaries, nested and empty ranges, and safe-break
behavior. Add coverage for repeated clusters, partial views, ligatures,
and negative letter spacing in both directions.

Lab results confirm reduced cost for the measured workloads.

[Test] Migrate Android Java tests from @Ignore to @DisabledTest

Chromium's Android test runner does not filter JUnit @Ignore on the
host, so skipped instrumentation tests still launch on device shards
while Test Reviver and test health tools cannot run or track them.
Migrating these tests to @DisabledTest avoids wasted shard runs and
restores disabled-test execution and reporting.

Make replacing an unbounded element non-cancelable

When a widget shows a new unbounded element while another one is
active, RegisterActiveUnboundedElement() dismissed the previous one
through OnDismissed(), which fires a cancelable beforetoggle event. If
the page canceled it, the previous element stayed active while its
state was overwritten by the new element, leaving it without a surface.

Dismiss the previous element programmatically instead, like
hideUnboundedElement(), so the beforetoggle event is not cancelable.

WebXR: Keep previously rendered OpenXR layers in composition

When an OpenXR composition layer has already been rendered at least once
(!needs_redraw()) and is not redrawn on a subsequent frame
(!is_rendered()), ReleaseActiveSwapchainImages() skips releasing the new
swapchain image so it can be reused on the next frame, while xrEndFrame
must still include the layer so the OpenXR runtime continues displaying
its most recently released swapchain image.

Also update OpenXrTestHelper to track the last released swapchain
texture index in xrReleaseSwapchainImage and read from it during
OnPresentedFrame rather than the newly acquired texture index, and
re-enable WebXrVrOpenXrBrowserTest.TestMediaLayers.

[crubit] Document layering issues in `rust_api_from_cpp.md`.

`rust_api_from_cpp` parses C++ headers when generating the bindings, so
it requires correct and complete GN dependencies.  `cxx` could get away
with missing dependencies (since GN does not check generated files by
default, and since many Chromium targets are big and monolithic).

This CL adds a "Dependency cycles and missing dependencies" section to
the "Troubleshooting" part of `rust_api_from_cpp.md`.  The new section
explains the background, links to https://crbug.com/558554239 and to
the Chrome browser modularity guidelines, and suggests moving C++ APIs
called from Rust into smaller targets.

Move ExportedCanvasResource creation to PushFrameIfNeeded

Behaviour change:

Now that we create ExportedCanvasResource sooner it's ctor and dtor will
run in cases where it didn't run before:

* should_call_push_frame is false
  should_call_push_frame can be false only if GetResourceForPushFrame
  returns null and is old artifact of some clients calling PushFrame
  with null and some don't.
* Size().IsEmpty()
  There are some edge cases where it's possible. ExportedCanvasResource
  ctor is not doing anything meaningful[1]. dtor will call
  CanvasResource::DropRefOnOwningThread[2], which will be either no-op
  for cases that use ExternalCanvasResource[3], or it will recycle
  resource [4][5], which is fine, as there is nothing bad happened with
  the resource.

[1]
https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/main:third_party/blink/renderer/platform/graphics/exported_canvas_resource.cc;drc=cc15068433e8d7284264b4fc0e2379c26210bdbd;l=16
[2]
https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/main:third_party/blink/renderer/platform/graphics/exported_canvas_resource.cc;drc=cc15068433e8d7284264b4fc0e2379c26210bdbd;l=25
[3]
https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/main:third_party/blink/renderer/platform/graphics/canvas_resource.h;drc=1647e0211f89061d9256af595096747d5ccdb3e1;l=65
[4]
https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/main:third_party/blink/renderer/platform/graphics/canvas_2d_resource_provider.cc;drc=1647e0211f89061d9256af595096747d5ccdb3e1;l=129
[5]
https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/main:third_party/blink/renderer/platform/graphics/canvas_non_2d_resource_provider.cc;drc=1647e0211f89061d9256af595096747d5ccdb3e1;l=482

[Runtime Mutability] Update comments and PlatformFieldTrials overrides

Updates outdated comments and TODOs related to runtime-mutable features
across base/ and components/variations/:
- Clarifies in base/feature.h that runtime-mutable features are
  currently supported in the browser process only (with
  crbug.com/536851532 tracking child-process support).
- Updates references from "main thread" to "main sequence" and clarifies
  thread-safety vs. sequence-affinity requirements in FeatureList and
  field_trial_params.h.
- Notes that the FeatureParam internal parsed value cache is bypassed
  for BASE_RUNTIME_MUTABLE_FEATURE features.
- Fixes stale symbol/type references in comments (e.g.,
  PlatformFieldTrials::EnableRuntimeMutableFeatures(), runtime override
  info, and nullptr).
- Updates the platform-specific overrides of
  PlatformFieldTrials::EnableRuntimeMutableFeatures() (in
  ChromeBrowserFieldTrials, AwFieldTrials, and IOSChromeFieldTrials) to
  call the base class implementation.

Reland "[ash] Drop dead profile.h includes" (3/4: apps)

This is a reland of commit 499ae8c51418fbcc82eb1465ed67061837c71c97,
split into four CLs by directory. This part covers
chrome/browser/ash/app_list, app_mode, arc and system_web_apps: 33
includes across 33 files, no DEPS or build changes.

These files include chrome/browser/profiles/profile.h but never name
Profile: the include survived whatever once used it. Candidates were
removed wholesale, then chrome, unit_tests, browser_tests and
interactive_ui_tests were built, and everything the compiler rejected
was put back.

The original was reverted over two scanning crosier tests that use
Profile without ever spelling it. They sit in a crosier_tests target
under is_chromeos_device, which none of those four targets build, so the
compiler never saw them. They keep their include and appear in none of
the four parts.

Android: Add on-device WPR benchmark runner

Add a config-driven Android instrumentation APK that runs WPR
benchmarks without host orchestration.

The runner starts WPR, configures browser flags through UiAutomation,
and controls Chrome through its local DevTools socket. A packaged relay
runs under the debuggable browser's UID to support CDP connections with
SELinux enforcing.

Support Crossbench-style page definitions for navigation, JavaScript,
touch, and wait actions, with configurable trace collection, result
processing, and file exports.

Provide on-device LoadLine2 trace processing. Speedometer 3.0 and
JetStream 3.0 examples extract results through configured JavaScript
actions. Results can be printed to logcat or exported as JSON and trace
files.

Benchmark definitions and dependencies are supplied through GN
configuration, allowing custom on-device WPR tests without modifying
the runner. Example definitions use placeholder dependency paths;
users provide their own benchmark assets.

[BottomBar] Add IPH_AndroidBottomBarEducationTooltips FET feature

The bottom bar opt-in dialog hands its tooltip tour to the recreated
activity through a SharedPreference, so the tour runs outside Feature
Engagement and other IPHs can show on top of it.

Add an FET feature for the tour, gated on a new
android_bottom_bar_education_opt_in_accepted event. The tour normally
starts right after the recreate. If that's missed, it can still start
on a later visit within 360 days, so a user who opted in gets it
eventually. It shows at most once per 360 days and blocks other IPHs
while it runs. Like the other bottom bar IPHs, the feature is disabled
by default and enabled through Finch.

Also make IPH_AndroidBottomBarEducation count toward the session rate,
so session-limited IPHs such as IPH_NewTabPageThemeCustomization don't
show in the same session, including after the activity recreate.

A follow-up CL will send the event from the dialog and move the tour
off the pref.

[Graduation] Fix midnight_timer_ tight loop on DST fall-back days

GetNextDayLocalMidnight() computed the next day's local midnight as
(date.LocalMidnight() + base::Days(1)).LocalMidnight(). On a 25-hour DST
fall-back day, adding a fixed 24 hours to date.LocalMidnight() lands at
23:00 on the same calendar day, causing LocalMidnight() to round back
down to today's 00:00 (in the past).

Whenever HasUpcomingGraduationEnablementChange() was true on a DST
fall-back day, MaybeScheduleAppStatusUpdate() scheduled midnight_timer_
for a timestamp in the past, causing OnMidnightTimer() to tight-loop for
the entire 25-hour day.

Add 28 hours to date.LocalMidnight() before rounding down to local
midnight so that 25-hour DST fall-back days advance to the next calendar
day.

[toolbar] Remove reload menu overrides that repeat the defaults

ReloadButton and WebUIReloadControl both override IsCommandIdChecked(),
IsCommandIdEnabled(), and IsCommandIdVisible() to return false, true,
and true. ui::SimpleMenuModel::Delegate already returns exactly those
values[1].

Both classes reach that delegate only through ReloadControl, which
doesn't override these methods[2]. ReloadButton's other base,
ToolbarButton, isn't a menu delegate[3][4]. The WebUI copies came with
the WebUI reload button's context menu[5].

Delete the six overrides. No behavior change.

This may clash with WIP prototypes[6][7][8].

Found and drafted with Jetski, using pauladedeji@'s cruft-sweep skill.
Each safety claim above links its evidence.

[1] https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/e2ec36d92fa24cf8cc5b80b95ed2c462c93af040:ui/menus/simple_menu_model.cc;l=29-39
[2] https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/e2ec36d92fa24cf8cc5b80b95ed2c462c93af040:chrome/browser/ui/views/toolbar/reload_control.h;l=13-28
[3] https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/e2ec36d92fa24cf8cc5b80b95ed2c462c93af040:chrome/browser/ui/views/toolbar/reload_button.h;l=37
[4] https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/e2ec36d92fa24cf8cc5b80b95ed2c462c93af040:chrome/browser/ui/views/toolbar/toolbar_button.h;l=51-52
[5] https://crrev.com/c/6998494

[omnibox][webui] Re-enable QueryWithTabContext on Windows and macOS

Re-enable `OmniboxAimWebUiInteractiveTest.QueryWithTabContext` on both
Windows and macOS:

- Windows: crrev.com/c/8628167 disabled `QueryWithTabContext` on Windows
  because `pixel_interactive_ui_tests` on CQ bypassed Skia Gold
  (`--bypass-skia-gold-functionality`, crbug.com/574560342) when
  crrev.com/c/8616998 landed, leaving the deterministic Windows digest
  (`bb123d7aeac4fab264a23f190e683d56`) for
  `..._AimPopupQueryWithTabContext_8616998_windows` untriaged on
  post-submit CI. That digest is now triaged as positive in Skia Gold
  and CQ Skia Gold verification is active (crrev.com/c/8593869).
- macOS: Pass a 1-second timeout to `CopyFromSurfaceSecure()` in
  `TabContextualizationController::CaptureScreenshot` instead of an
  infinite timeout (`base::TimeDelta()`). On macOS, when a background
  tab is hidden or resized before its renderer submits a compositor
  frame for the newly allocated `LocalSurfaceId`,
  `DelegatedFrameHost::CanCopyFromCompositingSurface()` still returns
  `true` while Viz holds the `PendingCopyOutputRequest` waiting for a
  surface at the new ID. A 1s timeout prevents `GetPageContext()` from
  stalling for 60s until `OnTabContextFetchTimeout` aborts the tab
  context upload.

views: Remove kSkipAccessibilityPaintChecks

The property let a View opt out of RunAccessibilityPaintChecks(), with
a TODO asking for it to be removed once the offending Views were fixed.

MessageBoxView has set it on its prompt Textfield since the checks were
first enabled (r928920): ChromeDriverTest.testSendTextToAlert opens
window.prompt() with no message, so the focusable field ended up with
an empty accessible name and NameFrom::kNone, which the checks reject.
A non-empty message has always been used as the field's name. Mark the
name explicitly empty when there is no message, the same way
IconLabelBubbleView and ContentSettingImageView handle an optional
name, so the checks pass without the property. The field also stays
hidden and ignored until a prompt is shown. Add unit tests for both the
named and the empty case that run the paint checks on a shown Widget.

The app-menu footer and block buttons set the property on their
ImageView and Label children. Those are never focusable and are marked
ignored, and the checks return early for unfocusable Views before
looking at anything else, so the property had no effect there.

Remove the key, the early return that read it and the remaining
SetProperty() calls, and drop the comment suggesting the key could be
turned into a cascading property.

Preloading: Remove AndroidPrerenderManager init

The native AndroidPrerenderManager class has no member state and only
forwards startPrerendering and stopPrerendering calls to the tab's
NewTabPagePreloadPipelineManager, while init() allocated a new C++
instance on the heap that was never freed.

Make StartPrerendering and StopPrerendering static methods invoked
directly from JNI without allocating a native peer or storing a raw
long pointer in Java.

WebUIExtensionsContainer: Fix WebAppFrameToolbarInteractiveUITest

The test CHECKed that the WebUI extensions container was disabled, but
the web app frame toolbar always uses the Views-based
ExtensionsToolbarDesktop regardless of that feature. As a result, the
CHECK crashed every test in the file when WebUIExtensionsContainer was
enabled.

Remove the CHECK (and the now-unused ui_features.h include) and document
why the Views container is always used here.

Verified all 6 tests pass both with and without
--enable-features=InitialWebUI,WebUIExtensionsContainer.

vr: refuse inotify in the XR process on Linux

Turnip, Mesa's Vulkan driver for Adreno GPUs, sets up tracing with
inotify_init1() when a Vulkan device is created in the XR process.
XrProcessPolicy falls back to the GPU process policy, whose baseline
crashes on inotify, so the XR process was killed ("seccomp-bpf failure
in syscall nr=0x1a") when a session started.

Return EPERM for inotify_init() and inotify_init1() instead. Turnip then
runs without that tracing.

[iOS][Autofill AI] Show SPII disclaimer IPH on suggestion chips

Ambient Autofill surfaces suggestions extracted by Gemini from personal
context sources such as Gmail and Google Photos, including sensitive
personally identifiable information (passports, driver's licenses, and
national ID cards). Users have no upfront reminder before
filling to verify sensitive values against the original source or that
long-pressing the chip shows source details.

Enable IPH_AutofillAmbientAutofillSpiiDisclaimer on iOS (renaming the
C++ symbol to kIPHAutofillAmbientAutofillSpiiDisclaimerFeature to match
iOS FET naming conventions) and attach a one-time IPH bubble to Personal
Context SPII suggestions in the Keyboard Accessory reminding users that
Gemini can make mistakes and pointing out that long-pressing the
suggestion opens the original source to verify accuracy.

[Docs] Update Spotlight exclusion steps in Mac and iOS build docs

Update the macOS and iOS build instructions with current steps for
excluding the Chromium checkout directory from Spotlight indexing.

In macOS 13 (Ventura), Apple replaced System Preferences with System
Settings and moved the Spotlight exclusion list under Siri & Spotlight
(or Spotlight) -> Spotlight Privacy... (or Search Privacy...).
Previously, docs/mac_build_instructions.md still documented the removed
pre-Ventura System Preferences path, and docs/ios/build_instructions.md
lacked Spotlight exclusion instructions altogether despite iOS builds
also running on macOS and generating a large number of files that slow
down builds when indexed by Spotlight.

No tests are added because this CL only updates markdown documentation.

[ios] Add overloads of BuildServiceInstanceFor(...)

In order to incrementally transition KeyedService factories to pass
ProfileIOS by reference instead of pointer, it will be necessary to
have two overloads of BuildServiceInstanceFor(...).

Factories that have not been converted to override the new version
BuildServiceInstanceFor(ProfileIOS&) will inherit the default that
forward the call to BuildServiceInstanceFor(ProfileIOS*).

Factories that have been converted to override the new version will
never call the default BuildServiceInstanceFor(ProfileIOS*) but if
it is called then it will fail with NOTREACHED().

3765ea0a57b77651bd743384f726f0f301c9a17a [ diff ] 
Do not activate hidden tabs when dragging a collapsed tab group

When dragging a collapsed tab group header within the tabstrip,
TabDragController was previously selecting all tabs in the group and
activating the first tab in the group both during drag initialization
(in ResetSelection) and upon drag completion (in CompleteDrag). Because
collapsed tab groups are prevented from expanding during a drag, this
resulted in an invisible tab inside the collapsed group becoming the
active tab and the previously active tab losing selection.

This CL ensures that neither ResetSelection nor CompleteDrag selects or
activates tabs in a dragged group if the group is collapsed, keeping the
existing active tab unchanged.

Also adds assertions to DragCollapsedGroupHeaderRemainsCollapsed in
tab_drag_controller_interactive_uitest.cc verifying that the active tab
remains unchanged and that no tab inside the collapsed group is
activated.

4bcca1dc44c8e149ce9dfe86bfd7a25fbbcbac3f [ diff ] 
[test] Run StorageService in-process in fast test builds

Every InProcessBrowserTest creates a default profile whose
StoragePartition initializes DOMStorageContextWrapper and launches an
out-of-process StorageService utility process. Across a typical
browser_tests shard, spawning, initializing, and tearing down a separate
storage_service_utility process per test accounts for ~2.5-3.5% of total
process CPU time.

In fast test builds (!EXPENSIVE_TEST_LOGIC_IS_ON(), i.e. when
dcheck_always_on is false or enable_expensive_dchecks is false), have
InProcessBrowserTest::SetUp() call
content::ForceInProcessStorageServiceForTesting() so the StorageService
runs on the browser IO thread (matching Android's configuration) instead
of spawning a separate child process.

Keep the out-of-process StorageService in DOMStorageMigrationBrowserTest
(which tests sandboxed out-of-process LevelDB-to-SQLite migration) and
ChromeMainDelegateHangWatcherTest (which verifies HangWatcher startup
histograms on a sandboxed utility process) via
set_force_in_process_storage_service(false).

[LongScreenshots] Allow skipping memory checks on all Android versions

kLongScreenshotsNoMemoryCheck previously bypassed memory checks only on
Android 16+ (Baklava), falling back to critical memory threshold checks
on older Android versions. This prevented evaluating capture completion
rates without memory checks across pre-Baklava devices.

The version restriction was added to avoid a ScrollCaptureConnection NPE
crash (crbug.com/278379299). However, LongScreenshotsTabService is used
only for the in-app long screenshot flow and does not interact with the
system ScrollCapture framework, making it unaffected by
crbug.com/278379299. Removing the Android 16 check allows
kLongScreenshotsNoMemoryCheck to bypass memory checks safely across all
Android versions.

[Views] Guard against menu items being deleted mid-insertion.

There are certain corner cases in which callbacks generated by menu
item insertion synchronously to accessibility API listeners could
conceivably destroy the menu (and the item) from underneath in the
middle of the insertion.

This blocks the destruction of any MenuItemView mid-insertion via a flag
which - if set - causes any attempt to destroy that view to CHECK().

Advantages of this approach:
 - Handles even unforeseen/future code paths that could lead to
   synchronous self-destruction.
 - Avoids any possibility of UAF since the object is valid up until the
   CHECK().
 - Provides a way to detect any malicious or buggy accessibility code
   incorrectly using this API in the wild.

Potential future work:
 - Add re-entrancy and destruction guards for any AddChildView
   operations.
 - Consider making AX tree change callbacks async to avoid the risk of
   such re-entrancy.

[scroll-snap] Apply the multicol scroll origin to ::column snap areas

A snap area rect is mapped to the snap container with
kIgnoreScrollOffset, which adds the scroll origin of each scroll
container the mapping steps into. For a normal snap area, the mapping
starts at the snap area, inside the scroll container. For a ::column,
it starts at the multicol container itself, so if the multicol
container is a scroll container, its scroll origin is never added.

In RTL, the scroll origin is non-zero, so every column snap position
was off by -ScrollOrigin() and clamped to the far end: a multicol
carousel opened on its last column and always snapped back to it.

terminalPrivate: Fix flake in OnProcessOutputSendToCorrectRenderer

Navigating to `chrome-untrusted://crosh/` with an empty path resolves to
`html/terminal.html` in `TerminalSource::StartDataRequest`, which in
browser tests loads `/js/terminal.js` and asynchronously invokes
`chrome.terminalPrivate.openVmshellProcess()`.

In `OnProcessOutputSendToCorrectRenderer`, this caused `tab2` to open its
own vmshell process during page load. When that process exited (or
emitted startup output) after `BROWSER_TEST_WAIT_FOR_LOAD_STOP` and
after `tab2` registered its `onProcessOutput` listener, `tab2` received
an `onProcessOutput` event from its own vmshell process and incremented
`window.processOutputCount` to 1.

Navigate both tabs to `chrome-untrusted://crosh/html/crosh.html` (as in
`OpenCroshProcessChecks`) so `TerminalSource` serves an empty test page
without spawning background `vmshell` processes.
