[password_manager] Simplify CSVFieldParser

Replace CSVFieldParser's 6-state machine and separate HasMoreFields() /
NextField(std::string_view*) methods with a single NextField() returning
std::optional<base::expected<std::string_view, SyntaxError>>.

The state machine (kBeforeField, kInsideRaw, kQuoted,
kAfterClosingQuote, kAfterLastField, kError) and character-by-character
UpdateState()/ConsumeChar() helpers were unnecessary:
- kInsideRaw, kQuoted, and kAfterClosingQuote only existed within a
  single NextField() call, since NextField() always consumes a complete
  field before returning.
- Unquoted fields (those not starting with '"') simply span up to the
  next ',' or end-of-row (even in the old state machine, kInsideRaw
  treated '"' like any other non-comma character), so they can be
  sliced directly with std::string_view::find(',').
- Quoted fields (starting with '"') only need a local bool in_quotes
  while scanning: inside quotes, '"' toggles in_quotes to false;
  outside quotes, '"' is an escaped quote (toggling in_quotes back to
  true), ',' terminates the field, and any other character is a syntax
  error.
- Inter-call state (kBeforeField vs. kAfterLastField vs. kError) is
  fully represented by std::optional<std::string_view> rest_, which is
  reset to std::nullopt once the final field is consumed or an error
  occurs (while an empty string_view after a trailing ',' yields the
  final empty field).

This is a pure refactoring; parsing behavior is unchanged.

`CrBrowserMain` before the `TracingService` utility process connects,
dropping events. Add `kPerfettoBrowserSharedMemorySizeBytes` (default
32 MB) and use it when `enable_consumer` is true in
`PerfettoTracedProcess::SetupClientLibrary`.

While a clean `about:blank` launch only buffers ~3 MB before
`TracingService` connects (~4.5s), a heavy Windows startup with session
and extension restore fills 4 MB in 2.1s (~2 MB/s) while
`TracingService` takes ~14-20s to spawn and drain the SMB, requiring the
full 32 MB (`kMaxShmSize`) to avoid a startup blind spot.

Tested: `StartupTracingTest` browser tests + verified 0 SMB data loss on
a 15 MB local `chrome --trace-startup=*` trace.

[a11y-android] Revert ignored check in IsNodeValid

crrev.com/c/8256250 added `!node->IsIgnored()` to `IsNodeValid` to
prevent crashes when operating on ignored nodes. However, using this
check in `WebContentsAccessibilityImpl.handleFocusChanged` causes
accessibility focus to reset to root during dynamic DOM and SPA
transitions when nodes are temporarily ignored.

crrev.com/c/8573418 subsequently added explicit ignored-node guards to
`PopulateAccessibilityNodeInfo`, `UpdateCachedAccessibilityNodeInfo`,
and `GetSelectionAsTextOffsetsForNode`, while `SetExtendedSelection`
remains guarded. `IsNodeValid` can therefore safely return to an
existence check (`GetAXFromUniqueID(id) != nullptr`).

A regression test is added to ensure operations on ignored nodes remain
properly guarded.

Webium: pass WaapUIMetricsService to InitialWebUINativeMetricsDispatcher

`InitialWebUINativeMetricsDispatcher` stored a `Profile*` and looked up
`WaapUIMetricsService::Get(profile_)` on every event. The
`InitialWebUIWindowMetricsManager` it reports to already caches the
service, so take the `WaapUIMetricsService*` directly in the constructor
instead.

Every `GetService()` caller in `InitialWebUIMetricsDispatcher` also
null-checked the service, which would silently drop metrics if it were
missing. A window with an `InitialWebUIWindowMetricsManager` always has
a `WaapUIMetricsService`, so CHECK it instead, including when
constructing `InitialWebUINativeMetricsDispatcher`.

To keep that true for a WebContents in the shared
`TopChromeWebUIProfile`, which has no `WaapUIMetricsService`,
`InitialWebUIWebContentsMetricsDispatcher::GetService()` now uses the
service of the window's profile instead of the WebContents' profile.

Both are the same profile today, since no WebUI uses
`TopChromeWebUIProfile` yet.

Reland "Android: support the macOS JDK layout for local builds"

This is a reland of commit 9791b17b69fb09bb582f500f92d3c4eac05ee13f

The original broke the chromium->v8 roller: V8 mirrors //build but not
//third_party/jdk, so isolates whose //build/android pydeps listed
//third_party/jdk/java_home.py failed to stat it. java_home.py now lives
in //build/android and jdk.gni in //build/config/android, so //build no
longer depends on files outside of it (ANGLE also ships its own
//third_party/jdk without jdk.gni).

Original change's description:
> Android: support the macOS JDK layout for local builds
>
> //third_party/jdk/current fetches jdk/${platform}, and the mac-arm64
> package keeps the .jdk bundle layout (current/Contents/Home/...), uses
> .dylib libraries and include/darwin headers, and lacks libawt_headless,
> libawt_xawt and libjsvml. Add //third_party/jdk/java_home.py as the
> single definition of the JDK home for Python, and
> //third_party/jdk/jdk.gni (android_jdk_home and the JDK input lists,
> moved out of config.gni) as its GN counterpart, and route
> //build/android, jni_zero and //third_party/jdk through them so Android
> builds work on macOS hosts. Linux is unchanged.
>

[cast] Add enable_harfrust flag and unify on C++ HarfBuzz shaping

Add an `enable_harfrust` build argument in
`third_party/harfbuzz/harfbuzz.gni` (defaulting to `true`) to allow
size-constrained embedded targets to exclude the experimental `harfrust`
Rust shaper while keeping the `font` and `skrifa` features of
`harfbuzz_rust` linked for Fontations support. Disable `enable_harfrust`
in `chromecast/build/args/config/linux.gni` to rely solely on the C++
HarfBuzz shaper on Linux Cast builds, saving ~645KB in binary size.

Test: Built third_party/harfbuzz and ran cast_graphics_unittests with enable_harfrust=false

[iOS] Re-enable NetworkTimeTrackerTest.UpdateFromNetworkNetworkError

NetworkTimeTrackerTest.UpdateFromNetworkNetworkError was disabled on iOS
in https://codereview.chromium.org/2449853005 when
NetworkTimeTrackerTest used a live net::EmbeddedTestServer and asserted
that an abruptly closed socket recorded -net::ERR_EMPTY_RESPONSE in the
NetworkTimeTracker.UpdateTimeFetchFailed histogram.

In https://crrev.com/c/3706690, NetworkTimeTrackerTest was migrated from
net::EmbeddedTestServer to an in-memory network::TestURLLoaderFactory
that deterministically injects a synthetic net::ERR_EMPTY_RESPONSE
completion status without performing real socket I/O. The test now
passes reliably on iOS.

Part of http://go/arthurmilchior-fix-all-test-skill-chrome for AI week.

[crypto] Tag TPM metrics keys on macOS and sweep leftovers

On Apple platforms, the startup TPM benchmark creates persistent
keychain keys with an empty application tag and deletes them when it
is done. A browser that exits mid-measurement leaves them behind, and
nothing ever removes them, so they pile up.

Give the benchmark keys their own tag, `<access group>.tpm-metrics`,
and delete any keys under that tag before each run. The tag is set in
//crypto so that the sweep never runs with an empty tag, which would
delete every untagged key in the access group.

The sweep still enumerates the whole access group, once per sampled
run.

[iOS] Re-enable QuickDeleteBrowsingDataTestCase.testSignOutFooterLink

In crrev.com/c/6242936 (relanded in crrev.com/c/6243286, bug 395061778),
QuickDeleteBrowsingDataTestCase.testSignOutFooterLink was disabled as
FLAKY_testSignOutFooterLink on simulators.

The test tapped the 'sign out of Chrome' link using a hardcoded
TapAtPointPercentage(0.95, 0.05) action intended to avoid tapping
empty whitespace when the link wrapped across two lines. However, on
single-line layouts (standard on modern iPhone and iPad screen widths),
tapping at y = 5% lands in the font ascent/margin above the character
glyphs, causing the tap to miss the link text on some simulator
configurations (notably MacOS 14 simulator bots) and leaving the test
timing out while waiting for the sign-out snackbar. Furthermore, the
test asserted that the footer was not visible immediately after
dismissing the signout snackbar before verifying that sign-out had
finished and without waiting for the data source section reload
animation to complete.

This CL resolves the flakiness by:
1. Dynamically checking whether the link element is multiline. If
   multiline, tap at (0.15, 0.75) to hit the wrapped link text on the
   second line; otherwise, use grey_tap() to hit the exact center of
   the single-line link.
2. Awaiting sign-out completion with [SigninEarlGrey verifySignedOut]
   before checking the footer visibility.
3. Waiting for the footer view to disappear asynchronously with
   waitForUIElementToDisappearWithMatcher: to allow the diffable data
   source animation to complete.
4. Removing the MAYBE_ macro and re-enabling the test.

Part of http://go/arthurmilchior-fix-all-test-skill-chrome for AI week.

[CodeHealth] Remove //third_party/android_media

We only use `//third_party/android_media` (an unmaintained 2013 Android
Support v4 sample) in `CafExpandedControllerActivity`, which opens when
tapping the media notification during video flinging. Meanwhile, normal
Presentation API casting (`CafNotificationController`) simply brings
the casting Chrome tab to the front.

This CL updates `RemotingNotificationController` to also bring the
casting tab to the front, and removes `CafExpandedControllerActivity`
along with `//third_party/android_media`.

Note: This is a minor behavioral change when tapping the notification
during video flinging, bringing the originating tab (which already has
in-page video controls) to the foreground instead of opening the legacy
fullscreen controller activity.

[Net] Fix thread races in SimpleCachePrioritizedEntryOrder

Fix and re-enable DiskCacheBackendTest.SimpleCachePrioritizedEntryOrder,
which was disabled for thread synchronization races in
crrev.com/c/1104383 and crrev.com/c/1105679.

The test had two race conditions between the main thread and the
sequenced worker `task_runner`:
1. `CreateEntryWithPriority()` completes optimistically while the disk
   creation task is still pending on `task_runner`, so `WriteData()`
   enqueues in `SimpleEntryImpl::pending_operations_` and only posts its
   worker task when `CreationOperationComplete()` runs on the main
   thread. A single `PostTaskAndReply()` only waited for the creation
   worker tasks, leaving the entries in `STATE_IO_PENDING` when
   `ReadData()` was called. Because `ReadData()` in `STATE_IO_PENDING`
   pushes to the FIFO `pending_operations_` queue instead of posting to
   `prioritized_task_runner_`, reads completed in FIFO order `{2, 3, 1}`
   instead of priority order `{3, 1, 2}`.
2. Even after all entries reach `STATE_READY`, calling
   `entry2->ReadData()` immediately wakes `task_runner`, which can begin
   executing entry 2's read before `entry3->ReadData()` and
   `entry1->ReadData()` are enqueued on the main thread.

Drain `task_runner` and the main-thread loop across the creation and
write phases so all three entries reach `STATE_READY`, and hold
`task_runner` with a `base::WaitableEvent` while queueing the three
`ReadData()` calls so they are prioritized deterministically.

Part of http://go/arthurmilchior-fix-all-test-skill-chrome for AI week.

[iOS] Remove empty Safe Browsing Standard Protection subpage

With both kMovePasswordLeakDetectionToggleIos and SBER deprecation
launched on iOS, the Safe Browsing Standard Protection subpage has no
remaining items and displays an empty table view when Standard
Protection is tapped a second time or via its info button:

- Clean up kMovePasswordLeakDetectionToggleIos (crbug.com/444244681),
  which has been enabled by default in Stable since M138, removing the
  feature flag definition and legacy disabled-flag code paths in
  Privacy settings and tests.
- SBER deprecation on iOS originally launched under the iOS-specific
  kExtendedReportingRemovePrefDependencyIos flag, which was enabled by
  default and removed in https://crrev.com/c/7256716 in favor of the
  cross-platform kExtendedReportingRemovePrefDependency flag. Remove
  the remaining iOS Settings checks for
  kExtendedReportingRemovePrefDependency and
  IsExtendedReportingDeprecated().
- Remove the now-unused SafeBrowsingStandardProtectionCoordinator,
  Mediator, ViewController, Consumer, navigation commands, and unused
  IDS_IOS_SAFE_BROWSING_STANDARD_PROTECTION_* strings, and configure
  the Standard Protection cell to match No Protection (only showing an
  info button when enterprise-managed).
